cases.name: a version 1 entry after migrate
cases.why: a chain that ends in migrate is closed: the entry after it is invalid

cases.name: migrate signed by a removed device
cases.why: v1 device 1 was removed in entry 3, so the migrate entry is invalid

cases.name: migrate with another op
cases.why: an entry with migrate carries no other op, except a recovery-signed entry's set-recovery

cases.name: a version 2 genesis that names the identity, but that migrate doesn't name
cases.why: migrate's `to` is another genesis's hash: this one is a stranger

description: Migrating from wire version 1 (SPEC §6.8). The version 1 chain is ../chain.json's four entries, validated by version 1.0's rules (Ed25519, context "tieroute/v1"); a current version 1 device appends a `migrate` op naming the hash of the version 2 genesis. The version 2 genesis is signed with a new composite device key only, commits to recovery key 1 of a new recovery code, v2/recovery.json's, since the version 1 code doesn't carry over (SPEC §6.8), and names the version 1 identifier in `migrated-from`. A client accepts the pair only if both links check out. Each case gives a version 1 chain and a version 2 genesis (signed text), and whether the pair is accepted.

keys.v1_devices: ../chain.json (device 3 is current at the v1 head; device 1 was removed in entry 3)

migrate_note: a version 1 entry: signed by v1 device 3 over JCS(["tieroute/v1", t, b]), with ops [{op: migrate, to: SHA-256 of the v2 genesis signed text}]
